History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
19-year-old female university student with 5-7 day history of dysuria, urinary frequency, lower suprapubic discomfort, and new pink-tinged urine—clinically consistent with uncomplicated cystitis (probable UTI).

History:
• Onset: Symptoms began just under 1 week ago.  
• Presenting complaints: Burning/stinging with micturition, increased urinary frequency, suprapubic aching pain (worse while voiding), noted pink discoloration of urine today.  
• No flank/back pain, no fever, no nausea/vomiting.  
• Bowel habit: Long-standing variable bowel pattern attributed to IBS; no acute change.  
• Gynecologic/sexual: On combined OCP; sexually active with long-term boyfriend; last unprotected intercourse 1–2 weeks ago; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; denies abnormal vaginal discharge.  
• No urinary incontinence, costovertebral tenderness, or systemic symptoms reported.  
• ROS otherwise unremarkable.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable Bowel Syndrome – variable stool consistency and frequency; uses antispasmodic for cramps.  
• No history of recurrent UTIs, renal disease, or other chronic conditions mentioned.

Medications:
• Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Mebeverine (presumed) for IBS – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
• Clindamycin – adverse reaction (details not specified).

Social History:
• Lives in university halls with a flatmate; first-year English student.  
• Non-smoker; tried cannabis once 1.5 weeks ago.  
• Drinks alcohol socially.  
• Sexually active with long-term partner; no condom use; on OCP.

Family History:
• No known bladder, kidney, or other relevant hereditary disorders reported.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during virtual consult; no vitals provided.

Investigations:
• Planned: Mid-stream urine (MSU) for dipstick, microscopy, culture & sensitivity.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Probable uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).  
  • Start oral antibiotic – options discussed: Nitrofurantoin 3-day course or Trimethoprim (exact regimen pending prescription).  
  • Provide MSU sample today for culture to guide therapy.  
  • Encourage oral hydration.  
  • Analgesia: Paracetamol as needed.  
  • Safety-net: Return/seek care if fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, or symptom persistence >1 week.

Issue 2: Chronic IBS – stable.  
  • Continue current antispasmodic medication.  
  • No change in management at this time.

General Plan items:  
  • Review urine culture results and adjust antibiotics if resistance noted.  
  • Consider pregnancy test if symptoms persist despite therapy given recent unprotected intercourse, although LMP 2 weeks ago and on OCP.  
  • Reinforce avoidance of cannabis use for general health.

Quality checks:
• Missing elements: No vitals, physical exam findings, or detailed antibiotic regimen documented.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor fillers but clinical content intact.
